To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a system that can operate in bandwidth-scare environments to enable contribution-awareness in overlay broadcasting systems.

(1) the performance of a bandwidth-demanding overlay broadcasting system is significantly affected by the bandwidth of hosts, (2) the multi-tree framework can improve performance in such environments, and (3) the performance can be further improved by considering host contributions and applying appropriate heuristics.
we have designed and implemented an overlay broadcasting system that can operate in bandwidth-sparse environments, and can provide equitable performance for high-contributing hosts.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design and deployment of overlay multicast systems that enable equitable contribution awareness and performance in environments characterized by limited bandwidth, significant heterogeneity in host bandwidth, and asymmetric bandwidth.
the design of bandwidthdemanding applications using overlays in Internet environments with limited bandwidth and heterogeneity in outgoing link bandwidth.
designing overlay multicast systems that can operate in environments where bandwidth is scarce.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our heuristics improve system utilization by 10-30%, and the performance to high contributors by 30-100%, while providing equitable performance among hosts with similar bandwidth contribution.

we have shown the multi-tree framework can be extended to support bandwidth-demanding applications in bandwidth-scarc environments, and that the heuristics we designed can improve the performance for high contributors by 20-240% and enable equitable bandwidth allocation.
our work is an important step in the design and implementation of overlay broadcasting systems that can be deployed in bandwidth-scarse environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the heuristics are able to achieve a better balance between fairness and efficiency in a multi-tree framework.
we have demonstrated the viability of overlay broadcasting for bandwidth-scarce Internet environments.

our work is the first to consider the design of overlays in bandwidth-scarc environments, and that our heuristics enable the multi-tree framework to operate in such environments and provide good performance to all hosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of overlay multicast systems should be cognizant of the contribution awareness of hosts.

overlay broadcasting systems can be designed to consider host contribution to improve the performance to high contributors and achieve more equitable distribution of resources among hosts with similar contribution levels.
the multi-tree framework can be extended to enable equitable bandwidth distribution and good performance to high-contributing hosts in bandwidth-constrained environments.
